_note: V4.7b's break-up verb. The split is pro-rata among the sector's OTHER MAJORS -- its rivals divide the market (the first draft split to the body tier and the pin caught it: pro-rata receipts push body firms past BODY_SHARE_MAX, the escalation the tier boundary exists to make impossible). A sector whose only major is the target refuses the verb: no absorber means the split silently falls to the residual -- a sector lever wearing a firm's name. The major's headcount reads zero through the committed flag, and its market share moves with the rivals' live ratios. The gate is authored HERE and is its one live copy: the constants file's BREAKUP_MIN_SHARE duplicated it unread and was deleted at the ultra's find -- a session re-adding the constant brings a reason, per the project's dead-constant rule (companies-model section 2's own rule, rescoped to the verb scale). V5.3 majors (the parent's call): the gate reads the firm's weight among its sector's live majors (major_share >= 0.30, a STAND-IN for the author), not its share of the sector: at the real shares a major holds 0.3 to 4 % of its sector, and the old firm_share >= 0.10 offered the verb to nobody.

actions.name: Break Up the Firm
actions.summary: Competition law dissolves the champion. Its market share passes to its rivals; its payroll goes with it; it does not come back.
